chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What is the minimum limit of rukūʿ and sujūd?

So he said: You say, “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-ʿAẓīmi wa bi-ḥamdih” three times in rukūʿ, and “Subḥāna Rabbīya al-Aʿlā wa bi-ḥamdih” three times in sujūd. So whoever omits one, he has diminished one third of his salat (prayer), and whoever omits two, he has diminished two thirds of his salat (prayer), and whoever does not recite tasbīḥ, then there is no salat (prayer) for him.

So this report indicates that they only negated completeness and merit. Do you not see that they said: whoever omits one, he has diminished one third of his salat (prayer), and whoever omits two, he has diminished two thirds of his salat (prayer)? For were the matter not as we have mentioned, there would be no difference between failing to recite one of them such that it would invalidate the salat (prayer), and failing to recite all of them; and we have known that they differentiated between the two.

key_terms.الْكَمَالَ: completeness or perfection of the act
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: an expression of declaring Allah free from imperfection; tasbīḥ

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum tasbīḥ required in rukūʿ and sujūd according to Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the minimum tasbīḥ to be recited in rukūʿ and sujūd during salat (prayer). It indicates a legal distinction between omitting part of the prescribed remembrance and omitting it entirely, showing that the wording about “no salat” is understood here in relation to completeness and excellence rather than absolute invalidity in every instance.
